main_statement.paraphrase: Hilbert-Smith in every dimension n >= 1 (n = 0 is trivial): no non-Lie locally compact group acts faithfully on a connected manifold. Stabilizers and fixed points are allowed; the manifold may be noncompact, nonorientable or nontriangulable. Excluded: manifolds with boundary (standard).

constructive_core.paraphrase: No faithful action of the p-adic integers on a connected manifold. This IS the known p-adic formulation (Lee 1997; Pardon 2013 intro); the headline follows from it by the classical reduction, which is cited, not re-proved (06-character-classes.tex:518-526).

headline_corollaries.paraphrase: Pardon's Conjecture 1.4: an almost periodic homeomorphism of such M has an iterate that is the time-one map of a continuous R-flow.

main_statement.note_for_comparator: No Lean. The headline equals the standard conjecture statement up to standard hypotheses (second countable group, Hausdorff second-countable manifold without boundary). Thm main is exactly the standard p-adic reduction target. Known cases cross-checked: n <= 2 classical, n = 3 Pardon 2013 (paper cites Thm 1.5), Lipschitz (Repovs-Scepin), quasiconformal (Martin), Holder (Maleshich), symplectic C^0-Hamiltonian (Shelukhin). The paper claims all n uniformly; the low-dimensional cases are not used.
main_statement.catalog_summary_check: CONTENTS.md:7512 says 'connected finite-dimensional topological manifold'; the paper adds Hausdorff, second countable, without boundary. Faithful match.

proof_architecture.claim: Reduction: a non-Lie group acting faithfully contains Z_p (cited). Newman plus faithfulness give an open subgroup G = Z_p acting faithfully and orientation-preservingly on a connected invariant chart subset O of R^n.

Stabilize to W = O x R^{d-n} with d odd >= 3, d > n. Collapse c: S^d -> W^+ and orbit map q: W^+ -> Y = W^+/G. Haar-averaging a ball pinch over a small open subgroup gives a: Y -> S^d with deg(aqc) = 1. This is the only use of small subgroups.

Witt groups E_d(X) = W_d(T(X)) of categories generated by proper pushforwards along ARBITRARY continuous maps from compact polyhedra. Verdier duality restricts to T; E is homotopy invariant (Woolf's cylinder) and has Balmer-Walter localization, a germ description of quotients, open-cover density, and dense doubling.

Fixed lattice: compare with the semialgebraic subcategory P via a Mayer-Vietoris induction over spheres with a uniform 2-power bound. P has integral generic signatures, so im E_d(S^d) lies in L_d^{-1} Z u_d with L_d = 2^{e_d}, and E_d(S^d)_Q = Q u_d. Odd d makes E_d(X) -> W_d(T(X)/T(U)) an integral isomorphism for contractible open U, and a degree-s map acts by s rationally.

Character classes: the orbit sheaf q_*C splits into eigensheaves for Lambda = mu_{p^infty}; the projectors are self-adjoint off b = t(y_inf). For a finite partition, z_i(t) is the integral lift of [A,alpha] + [A, alpha(2e_i-1)] from the quotient by objects supported near b. Sum = 2[A,alpha]; covariant; homotopy invariant via the close-pair space C_d.

Concentration: faithfulness gives, for each k, a region V where W/p^kG -> W/G has p^k labelled sheets and a multiplier beta. Rational orbit injectivity plus odd-sphere rationalization give h ~ D_s a with h constant off V. Multiplication by beta cyclically permutes the transversal partition D_i = zeta^i D_0, so z_i(h) are all equal.

Contradiction: s * z̄_i(a) = z̄_i(h) for all i, so the z̄_i(a) are equal. Their sum is 2 * 2 * deg(aqc) u_d = 4 u_d, so each z̄_i(a) = (4/p^k) u_d. That lies outside L_d^{-1} Z u_d once p^k > 4 L_d, and L_d was fixed before k.

eureka_candidates.name: Integral character classes z_i(t) (localization-lifted 'twice the isotypic summand')
eureka_candidates.for: It is hard to anticipate an invariant that is (a) integral, (b) defined for each character part of a profinite action with infinite-dimensional stalks, and (c) homotopy-invariant in the test map even though the decomposition fails at the fixed point at infinity. The trick [A,a] + [A,a(2e-1)] avoids splitting idempotents, and odd d makes the localization lift integral. It is not a subterm of the goal or of L, and every step of the contradiction runs through it. Rational or C-coefficient homology cannot do this: character splitting needs C, which loses integrality, whereas Witt groups of real forms keep integral signatures.
eureka_candidates.against: For finite groups, isotypic G-signature components are classical (Atiyah-Singer, equivariant Witt groups, Neumann's hermitian-representation Witt groups). The construction is formally the profinite, germ-localized version of a known invariant. A judge might grade it N2.
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour_quick_check: Quick searches found no use of Witt groups or signatures for Hilbert-Smith. The nearest known approaches are Williams' K-theory 'infinite product' programme for B Z_p (via Dranishnikov et al. 2015), Pardon's 3-manifold MCG argument and Shelukhin's Floer power operations. G-signature in Witt spaces (Banagl-Leichtnam-Piazza 2025) concerns compact Lie groups, not profinite ones.

eureka_candidates.name: Equal parts in a fixed lattice (fix L_d before k)
eureka_candidates.for: It reformulates the profinite 'Haar fractional degree' as p^k equal integral classes summing to 4, against a lattice fixed in advance. The order of quantifiers (L_d before k) is the crux. No precedent found for Hilbert-Smith.
eureka_candidates.against: The shape is the classical divisibility/transfer contradiction (Smith theory; degree divisible by |G|). The novelty lives in I42 and I26, not in the counting.
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour_quick_check: Classical transfer arguments (Borel/Bredon) and Yang's dimension raising use divisibility in Z/p cohomology. No Witt-integrality version was found.

eureka_candidates.name: Moving a positive multiple of the degree-one test into any open set of the orbit space
eureka_candidates.for: It works on orbit spaces with no dimension bound (the known theory says dim is n+2 or infinity), avoiding the classical obstacle. It bridges a global degree with local sheet symmetry.
eureka_candidates.against: Each piece is standard: rational transfer for compact groups, rationalization of odd spheres (the same telescope as Dranishnikov-Ferry-Weinberger 2003, cited) and homotopy extension.
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour_quick_check: DFW 2003 Prop 4.5 uses the identical telescope argument (cited by the paper).

eureka_candidates.name: Averaged degree-one test
eureka_candidates.for: It is the only use of small subgroups: an integral degree-one class on the wild orbit space, which is impossible for any finite group.
eureka_candidates.against: Haar averaging of maps or metrics is classical (Bochner-Montgomery; Repovs-Scepin average a metric). It is one step from L.
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour_quick_check: Repovs-Scepin 1997 averaged invariant metric; standard compact-group averaging.

eureka_candidates.name: Bounded (2-power) comparison F -> E on spheres; T categories generated by arbitrary continuous images
eureka_candidates.for: It extends sheaf Witt homology integrally to non-constructible objects, which the action forces on us. Rational equivalence alone would lose the denominator bound.
eureka_candidates.against: It is a standard comparison of homology theories via Mayer-Vietoris; the categories adapt Woolf 2008 and Ranicki-Weiss 2010 (both named by the paper).
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour_quick_check: Woolf 2008 (Comment. Math. Helv. 83): constructible Witt groups form a generalized homology theory on polyhedra and continuous maps.

correctness_audit.verdict: Line-by-line reading of all six sections and the appendix found NO gap. The logical skeleton is coherent and passes every 'proves too much' test I could construct. But this is an unreviewed claimed proof of a famous open conjecture, with no Lean and no trace, and it is surprisingly short (~3.5k lines). Treat it as UNVERIFIED pending expert review in sheaf-theoretic Witt groups and transformation groups.
checked: Chart reduction (05:23-73): the clopen argument for F_j = int Fix(H_j) is correct; Newman applies to N' = H_j B (connected, invariant, finite-order action); 2H handles orientation for p = 2.

Averaged test (05:152-183): uniform continuity on compact G x W^+ gives an open H moving points by less than the pinch scale; the normalized Haar average is homotopic to the pinch rel infinity, so deg(aqc) = 1. Correctly fails for finite groups, where H must be trivial.

Finite sheets (05:409-434): some x has G_x inside p^kG by the closed-subgroup classification plus faithfulness; the free orbit of z in W/p^kG gives disjoint translates; the beta equivariance is correct.

Move-test (05:491-516): aq is homotopic to a pinch inside q^{-1}V, so it is constant on q^{-1}F; rational orbit injectivity then gives (a|_F)^* gamma = 0; the odd-sphere telescope gives D_s a|_F nullhomotopic; homotopy extension finishes. Elementary cross-check: deg(hqc) = s must be divisible by m = p^k (the m clopen sheet preimages contribute equal local degrees), which is consistent with z̄_0(h) = 4s/m being in the lattice.
Germ theorem (03:179-219) and cutoff (03:42-110): the roof construction, the cone support in a compact subset of U, and faithfulness via ts = 0 are all correct.

Contractible quotient (04:504-529): E_d(U) = E_d(pt) = 0 for odd d; E_{d-1}(U) -> E_{d-1}(X) is split injective via the point; so the localization map is an integral isomorphism in both classes d = 1, 3 mod 4. This answers my initial worry that the boundary into W_{d-1}(T(U)) = Z for d = 1 mod 4 could obstruct lifting.
Dense doubling (03:364-460): D(q) = q + q + H(x[1]) lands in A via y + y[1] in A; the lagrangian L of D(q) + H(z) lies in A; i d = d i = 2. This is the known Hornbostel-Schlichting cofinality.
Bounded comparison (04:136-185) and the exponent recursion e_j = 9e_{j-1} + 6 are correct.
Real orthogonality (06:157-203): the adjoint computation D(i_E) alpha (T - M_lambda) = D(R_E) D(i_E) alpha is correct, with T^dagger = T^{-1} and M_lambda^dagger = M_{lambda^{-1}}.
Sum of classes (06:262-291): S = sum E_j P_j satisfies S^2 = 1, S^dagger = S and S^dagger Q_0 S = Q. The sum of twisted classes is (2-m)[A], plus m[A] gives 2[A].

Equal parts (06:421-443): T M_beta = M_{zeta^{-1}} M_beta T is correct, so beta cycles D_i to D_{i-1}. |beta| = 1 makes it an isometry of Re(z w̄). It is defined over S^d \ {b} because the source lies in q^{-1}V.
Homotopy of classes (06:350-391): the close-pair space C_d and the covariance plus pi_0 ~ pi_1 argument are correct.

Final arithmetic (06:470-499): [A_a, alpha_a] = 2(aqc)_* u_d has rational image 2u_d; the sum of z̄_i(a) is 4u_d; each is (4/p^k)u_d; this contradicts the lattice for p^k > 4L_d. The quantifier order (L_d independent of k and s) is respected.
consistency_checks_passed: Finite cyclic actions Z/m (e.g. a free rotation of (R^2 \ 0) x R^{d-2}): no degree-one test exists, since the degree is divisible by m on free regions, and the classes give 4c each, which is integral. No false contradiction.
Circle actions: no small subgroups, so the averaged test is impossible. No false contradiction.
Z_p actions on non-manifold compacta (Raymond-Williams): the machine needs the source over X \ {b} to be an open subset of S^d carrying an orientation form, so it does not apply.
Profinite actions such as (Z/p)^N, already excluded by Newman: the argument would also exclude them, which is consistent.

Witt-theoretic sanity: for a finite free action, each character part has local signature equal to deg(t) times its rank, so parts are equal and integral. For Z_p, each D_i part has infinite rank on free regions; the paper's invariant then assigns a Haar fraction 4/p^k, which the lattice forbids. This is exactly where the proof bites.
Coarsening consistency: formal additivity of z_D under unions makes the level-k and level-(k+1) transversal partitions compatible (p parts of 4/p^{k+1} make 4/p^k).
residual_concerns: EXTRAORDINARY CLAIM. Hilbert-Smith is open in dimension >= 4 per the literature to 2019; McAuley's 2001 claimed proof was not accepted. A ~25-page proof avoiding all dimension theory of orbit spaces is a red flag in itself, though I found no error.

The load-bearing new foundation is the Witt theory of T(X): non-constructible objects with infinite-dimensional stalks. Biduality is proved via proper pushforward (sound in my reading). But the full chain (Balmer-Walter hypotheses for T and its Verdier quotients, including TR4+, which is asserted to pass to quotients; the germ description; dense doubling in quotients) needs a specialist check. Any error here voids the lattice L_d, which is the crux.
Homotopy invariance for non-proper homotopies of non-compact test spaces (contractible U, I = S^{j-1} x R) relies on compact-support pushforward (02:733-735). It looks right but is used everywhere.

Prop. generic-signature: the sign of the induced H^0 pairing for degree-d forms in both odd classes mod 4 rests on Appendix A conventions (04:334-336). A sign slip would make the H^0 form alternating for one class of d, but d can be chosen freely, so this is not fatal.
The classical reduction to Z_p and the Balmer-Walter theorem are cited, not re-proved (standard and reliable).

Lemma odd-sphere-null cites a specific Serre corollary ('degree-2q map kills q-torsion'); I did not verify the exact locator, but rationalization of odd spheres as K(Q,d) is classical, so the conclusion is safe.
Nothing in this reading is machine-checked (no Lean). This family is the test case for the unformalized path: the audit is one careful reading, not verification.

extraction_friction: No Lean, so there is no comparator and no declaration DAG. Load-bearing judgements come from the LaTeX dependency structure only.

Key objects are defined in prose or display math, not environments: the orbit sheaf H and the eigensheaves H_lambda (06:25-35), the averaged map A (05:170-172), the multiplier beta (inside Lemma finite-sheets), the transversal partition D_i (06:396-402), the close-pair space C_d (inside a proof, 06:354-357), and the doubling form D(q) (inside a proof). Only 'faithful', 'almost periodic', 'test space' and 'compact test' are \emph-defined.

The headline (cor:lie) is labelled 'cor' but stated as a Theorem before thm:main. Its proof is a one-paragraph cited reduction at the very end (06:518-526). Extractors keyed on 'theorem' would mis-rank it.
The organising idea (equal parts in a fixed lattice) appears only in the introduction (01:163-181) as prose; I extracted it as I49.

Cue phrases: 'close antecedent' (Ranicki-Weiss), 'implements the interval argument of [Woolf]', 'follows from the cofinality theorem ... We give a direct proof', 'The same odd-sphere telescope ... are used in [DFW]'. These mark N0/N2 items reliably.
Field labelling: the problem is Topology, but the essential machinery is sheaf theory and hermitian K-theory. The field-flow signal is strong and clear-cut here.
